items.title: C-HAT-Bench: Benchmarking Chinese AI-Text Detection Beyond Fully Generated Text
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly participate in writing by modifying or extending human drafts, causing machine involvement to vary in both form and extent. Yet most Machine-Generated Text (MGT) detectors are evaluated only on fully human-written versus fully AI-generated text. Because human--AI collaboration can weaken or redistribute cues associated with machine generation, strong performance under this binary setting may overstate detector reliability. This mismatch remains underexplored in Chinese: detection cues are shaped by tokenization and language-specific text distributions, yet controlled resources spanning production settings, domains, and generators remain limited. To fill this gap, we present a Chinese Human-AI Collaborative Text Detection Benchmark (C-HAT-Bench), a unified benchmark that links $5,000$ human-written source texts from five domains to more than $240,000$ variants produced using six generative models under Prefix-Conditioned Continuation as a reference setting and three collaborative production modes. We evaluate $21$ detectors through four protocols spanning zero-shot and pretrained supervised document-level detection, boundary localization, and cross-condition generalization. Relative to Prefix-Conditioned Continuation, mean AUROC across document-level detectors is $12.0\%$ lower on the collaborative production modes, with the largest detector-specific relative decrease reaching $44.4\%$. Transfer across collaborative production modes is also asymmetric, indicating that performance in a given production setting is not a reliable predictor of performance in other production settings.

items.title: CAIRN: Dynamic Fact-Intent DAGs for Multi-Agent Exploration
items.abstract: LLM-powered autonomous systems have demonstrated promising capabilities in mathematical reasoning, engineering, and cybersecurity. Yet how to organize these systems for effective, reliable, and sustained performance remains an open question. In this paper, we present CAIRN, a fact-intent-driven multi-agent paradigm for goal-directed exploration. CAIRN represents observations and planned investigations as a dynamic directed acyclic graph (DAG). A reasoner interprets facts to propose intents, which workers execute to produce new facts. Each intent references its supporting facts and defines a potential exploration branch. The persistent graph preserves goals, dependencies and findings across workers, supporting knowledge reuse and parallel exploration. The graph also makes execution trajectories traceable and auditable, providing a basis for human verification and intervention. We evaluate CAIRN across cybersecurity and mathematical reasoning tasks, examining task success, time to solution, and token consumption. DAG-based coordination can incur higher token costs with no observable performance gains on tasks that require little effort. However, on high-effort tasks (at least 1M tokens), we observe faster solutions in 76.5% of cases, with speedups of up to 3.08x. Moreover, as task effort increases, these time gains become more pronounced while relative token overhead declines, highlighting the potential of DAG-guided parallel exploration.

items.title: Can Large Language Models Code Reality Criteria in Autobiographical Statements? Reliability and Validity of an Artificial Intelligence–Based Tool for Criteria-Based Content Analysis
items.abstract: Objective: Coding for Criteria-Based Content Analysis (CBCA) to differentiate fabricated from experience-based autobiographical statements is slow and depends on trained coders whose agreement is imperfect. We developed the large language model (LLM) based system CBC-AID and evaluate its reliability and validity in coding CBCA. Hypotheses: As preregistered, AI–human consistency is non-inferior to the interrater reliability of trained coders (H1: total score; H2: each criterion), and AI-based scores discriminate between experience-based and fabricated statements at least as well as human scores (H3: total score; H4: each criterion). Method: Two versions of an LLM-based coding tool (CBC-AID), a single-prompt and a multi-agent system, coded 957 transcripts from 399 persons in nine laboratory studies with human CBCA codings and known truth status. Bivariate Bayesian multilevel models estimated within-study correlations and standardized truth effects under global rating and weighted frequency. Results: AI–human correlations of the total scores (ρ = .53–.67) fell short of the benchmark of .66 in all four combinations of version and scoring scheme; Version 1 under global rating came closest (ρ = .67, 95% CrI [.62, .72]). The AI assigned higher scores than human coders (0.7–2.7 SD). Truth effects were similar for AI-based (δ = 0.17–0.32) and human coding (0.16–0.24; Δδ = −0.06 to 0.12); non-inferiority was supported for one of four combinations, and human coding itself discriminated weakly. Conclusions: LLM-based coding approximated but did not reach the consistency of trained coders and preserved their modest discriminative validity. It may serve as a traceable supplement to human coding in research; forensic use requires field validation and human oversight.

items.title: Can Open-Weight Large Language Models (LLMs) Simulate Human Survey Populations? A Cross-Instrument Calibration Study
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to generate synthetic survey respondents and digital twins of real people, but whether their output preserves real human statistical structure, rather than surface plausibility, remains unresolved, and most existing evidence comes from proprietary models rather than open-weight ones. We evaluate three open-weight LLM families on a cross-instrument calibration task: conditioning personas on real respondents' verbatim answers to one psychometric instrument and measuring them on a second, construct-distance-controlled instrument, checked against a 2,058-person human panel. Across a 139-pair grid, the simulated cross-instrument correlation tracks the real human correlation at r = 0.70 - 0.73 in every model, driven mainly by correct sign rather than precise magnitude and concentrated in pairs of moderate construct distance. A correlation of this magnitude, obtained from untuned open-weight models conditioned only on individual-level survey data, is a substantively encouraging result for LLM-based behavioral simulation and digital-twin applications: specific model families and releases already reproduce a meaningful share of real human cross-instrument structure without any fine-tuning. This capability does not, however, improve monotonically across model releases: on a matched panel, the newest of three tested Llama releases performs worst on two of three headline metrics, so realizing its promise in practice requires release-specific, distance-aware verification rather than a one-time benchmark.

items.title: Can there really be ethical robots for autistic children?
items.abstract: Abstract With the advancement of autonomous technologies such as AI-driven social robots, the academic discussions around ethical standards have intensified over the years. These discussions have resulted in increased emphasis on concepts such as safety, trust, privacy, human dignity and well-being along with variety of ethical frameworks proposed by scholars. In parallel with these technological developments, therapeutic interventions for autistic children assisted by AI and social robots have also attracted increased attention. Against this backdrop, this paper critically examines six social robotics projects funded under the EU’s Horizon 2020 initiative from an ethics perspective. The main aim of these completed projects was to develop AI-driven semi-autonomous technologies such as humanoid and non-humanoid robots to assist autism interventions. To address the ethical shortcomings of the said projects, this paper mobilizes perspectives from critical disability studies, critical autism studies and the autism community itself, particularly concerning the negative impact of interventions on autistic individuals as a neurominority group. Beyond the commonly addressed shortcomings in the field of AI and social robotics, the article highlights that the biggest shortcoming of these projects is the absence of critical reflection on the ethical acceptability of applying neuronormative behavioral interventions to a neurominority group. By situating robot-assisted interventions within the context of normalization and technoableism, the article points out the epistemic injustice and the harm that can be potentially enacted on autistic people through such technologically aided interventions. Ultimately, the paper questions whether ethical assistive technologies for autistic individuals can exist under these circumstances.

items.title: CAPEX: Efficiently Distilling Foundation Model Behavior into Deployable Robot Policies through Experience-Adaptive Reasoning
items.abstract: Robot learning has largely relied on human-teleoperated demonstrations to acquire effective learnable behaviors. However, human-operated data collection processes can be unintuitive, difficult to scale, and inherently asynchronous. We explore an alternative: distilling physical behavior from general-purpose multimodal foundation models into deployable robot policies by using the foundation model itself as an autonomous demonstrator. While sufficiently capable models can generate successful zero-shot manipulation trajectories, repeatedly invoking them during physical execution is slow and expensive, limiting their utility as scalable data generators. As a solution, we introduce CAPEX, an experience-conditioned demonstration collection framework that uses execution experience from previous attempts to adapt how frequently the foundation model must observe, reason, and replan. We evaluate across RoboCasa tasks and on physical Franka and bimanual YAM-arm platforms, measuring task success, model calls, token usage, collection time, and cost. We further train Diffusion Policy and ACT on matched sets of human-teleoperated and foundation-model-generated demonstrations to evaluate the downstream learning value of autonomously collected data. We find that CAPEX increases the number of successful demonstrations by 4.3x while reducing the cost per successful demonstration by 80%. Policies trained on CAPEX-generated data approach the performance of those trained on matched human demonstrations; with longer training, this gap largely closes for policies trained from scratch. These results suggest that foundation models can serve as scalable sources of reusable robot experience. Project page: https://capex-paper.github.io/

items.title: Challenges and Prospects of Integrating Artificial Intelligence into Assessment of Students Learning in Public Examinations in Nigeria
items.abstract: The incorporation of artificial intelligence (AI) into the assessment of student learning in public examinations in Nigeria presents an available opportunity for the education sector. This review examines the benefits, challenges, and imminent prospects associated with the use of AI grading of assessments in Nigeria, with a focus on improving the accuracy, objectivity and proficiency in public examinations such as the West African Senior School Certificate Examination (WASSCE) conducted by WAEC, Senior School Certificate Examination (SSCE) conducted by (NECO), and the Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination (UTME) conducted by JAMB. The major benefits of integrating AI into assessment of students learning include increased efficacy, objectivity, on-time feedback, consistency and ability to adapt to increase in numbers of students writing exams annually. These benefits can meaningfully improve the speed and reliability of learning assessment while accommodating a very large number of students or candidates. Conversely, some challenges must not be ignored, such as inadequate infrastructural resources, high initial costs implementing, ethical and data privacy concerns, and resistance to technological changes. To address these challenges, cooperation between the government and the private sectors, capacity development and healthy management of data are recommended. By implementing these methods, AI can create a more effective and reliable framework for assessing student learning. Therefore, this study explores the challenges and prospects of integrating artificial intelligence into assessment of students learning in public examinations in Nigeria.

items.title: Clarify the User or Verify the World? Uncertainty Routing for Proactive Agents
items.abstract: Tool-using LLM agents must decide not only whether additional information is needed, but also which source can resolve the uncertainty. Existing proactive approaches often specialize in either user clarification or environment verification, without explicitly determining the appropriate information source for each decision. We formulate this problem as uncertainty routing among ACT, CLARIFY, and VERIFY, and propose PROUR, a proactive uncertainty routing framework. PROUR decomposes action uncertainty into disagreement across plausible user-goal interpretations, which signals user-side ambiguity, and the entropy remaining within each interpretation, which signals missing world-side evidence. To acquire information from the routed source, a query generator is trained with a mode-conditioned information-gain reward, targeting user-goal identification under CLARIFY and next-action identification under VERIFY. On $τ$-bench, PROUR achieves 28.17% average success rate across retail and airline, outperforming the strongest prior method by 4.57% while using 2.17 fewer interaction steps. The learned policy further generalizes to stronger task agents and transactional domains of $τ^3$-bench without retraining, demonstrating the benefit of source-aligned uncertainty resolution for proactive agents.

items.title: Clinician-curated ChatGPT-4o– and DeepSeek-R1–assisted exercise programmes added to standard physiotherapy for subacromial pain syndrome: a triple-masked randomized controlled trial
items.abstract: Large language models may assist clinicians in developing exercise programmes and could offer an alternative approach to conventional physiotherapist-designed rehabilitation in musculoskeletal disorders such as subacromial pain syndrome. The aim of this triple-masked randomized controlled trial was to compare clinician-curated ChatGPT-4o– and DeepSeek-R1–assisted exercise programmes with a conventional physiotherapist-designed exercise programme in individuals with subacromial pain syndrome. This 3-arm randomized controlled trial was conducted in the outpatient physical medicine and rehabilitation clinic of a university-affiliated hospital. Adults aged 18 to 65 years with subacromial pain syndrome were randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio to receive conventional, clinician-curated ChatGPT-4o–assisted, or clinician-curated DeepSeek-R1–assisted exercise programming. All groups received identical physical therapy modalities and supervised exercise sessions 3 times per week for 6 weeks. The primary outcome was the Shoulder Pain and Disability Index. Secondary outcomes included pain during activity, Quick Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder and Hand, and the 12-Item Short Form Health Survey. Between-group comparisons were based on change scores from baseline to week 6. Seventy-five participants were enrolled, and 69 completed the 6-week follow-up. Shoulder Pain and Disability Index scores improved in all groups, with no significant between-group difference over 6 weeks ( P = 0.428). No significant between-group differences were found for key secondary outcomes after Holm adjustment, including pain during activity ( P = 0.744), Quick Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder and Hand ( P = 0.744), and physical component summary scores ( P = 0.374). Resting pain differed significantly between groups ( P = 0.005), favouring DeepSeek-R1 over conventional programming (mean difference, 2.74 [95% CI, 1.26 to 4.22]). No adverse events were reported. Clinician-curated ChatGPT-4o– and DeepSeek-R1–assisted exercise programmes did not produce superior 6-week improvements in shoulder pain-related disability or key functional outcomes compared with conventional programming in subacromial pain syndrome; these findings should not be interpreted as establishing equivalence. The observed resting-pain difference in favour of DeepSeek-R1 was exploratory and requires confirmation. Clinical trial registration : ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT07148687) First Posted 3 August 2025.

items.title: Co‐Evolution of Humans, AI, and Robotics in Autonomous Materials Manufacturing
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Materials manufacturing has entered into a new era with the rapid development of technologies. The convergence of artificial intelligence (AI) and robotics technologies is transforming materials manufacturing from a traditional human‐centered practice into a human, AI, and robotics co‐evolution paradigm. Here, co‐evolution extends beyond conventional human‐in‐the‐loop supervision through reciprocal adaptation: Humans define objectives and constraints and refine them in response to new discoveries; AI translates these objectives and accumulated knowledge into testable hypotheses and experimental plans, then uses new evidence to refine its models and research strategy; and robotic platforms execute experiments and are reconfigured in response to emerging experimental requirements. Such intelligent autonomous materials manufacturing not only accelerates the discovery‐to‐production cycle but also enhances reproducibility and resource efficiency. In this perspective, we discuss the evolution of materials manufacturing, highlighting the roles of robotic platforms and AI in enabling autonomous materials manufacturing, and present a general framework for the human‐AI‐robotics collaboration and co‐evolution paradigm. We further outline the key challenges and future pathways, including effective AI‐driven design, reconfigurable robotic systems, and the critical role of automated characterization.

items.title: Coarse Graining, Sampling Bias, and Emergent Dynamics: How Discretization Choices, Network Topology, and Stoichiometric Constraints Jointly Shape Inference in Biological Systems
items.abstract: This version corrects a citation error in the list of excluded papers. A paper on self-regulatory communication in evolved neural agents was listed under the identifier 2602.02840, which belongs to an unrelated paper on quadratic gravity; the correct identifier is arXiv:2606.02840. The paper was excluded from the synthesis, so no claim changes. This version corrects specific citation errors found by an automated check and confirmed by hand; it has not had a full claim-by-claim audit. The full list of corrections is at the top of the PDF. A recurring structural problem cuts across several recent preprints in molecular network biology, population genetics, and genomics: the inference tools we deploy to characterize biological systems introduce systematic distortions that are not random noise but are instead architectural, embedded in the discretization schemes, sampling distributions, or representational formalisms chosen at the outset. This paper synthesizes six findings from the q-bio corpus to argue that a coherent pattern is visible across scales, though not formally derivable from a single shared structure: (1) Boolean discretization of gene regulatory networks systematically suppresses intermediate dynamical behaviors including higher-order multistability and stable periodic orbits (arXiv:2606.14925); (2) uniform sampling of canalizing Boolean functions over parameters rather than over distinct functions exponentially suppresses high-sensitivity functions, biasing conclusions about network robustness and attractor structure (arXiv:2606.05196); (3) autocatalytic formalisms that appear mathematically incompatible, RAF sets and stoichiometric autocatalysis, share a common stoichiometric matrix representation, and under mild conditions any RAF is stoichiometrically autocatalytic, suggesting the apparent theoretical gap is at least partly an artifact of representational choice (arXiv:2605.25523); (4) a transformer-based foundation model for m6A RNA methylation demonstrates that reformulating the input representation (peak-derived priors rather than adenosine-centered windows) substantially reduces false positives and improves precision-recall performance, though a PR-AUC of 0.635 indicates meaningful false positives remain (arXiv:2606.12219); (5) spatial context is a non-ignorable variable in cell-level gene expression inference, and treating cells as i.i.d. introduces counterfactual errors correctable by explicit disentanglement of intrinsic state from neighbor context (arXiv:2606.08493); and (6) elemental stoichiometry across metabolomes appears to occupy a statistically distinct region of chemical space relative to synthetic and planetary chemistry samples, though this distinction depends on standardized data-collection methods, suggesting that the statistical envelope of molecular composition may be a candidate biosignature (arXiv:2605.19252). This is a heuristic reading, not a derivation: the six findings do not share a single formal structure, but they share a common inferential failure mode, conclusions that depend on representation are being treated as conclusions about biology. The primary falsification path is stated per claim. Sources are drawn from q-bio.MN, q-bio.GN, q-bio.BM, and q-bio.PE preprints from May-June 2026. items.title: Combinations of menu types, interaction methods, and performance metrics in virtual reality: a systematic review
items.abstract: Virtual reality (VR) applications rely on menu interfaces to support effective interaction. However, evidence on how menu type, interaction method, and performance metrics relate to VR menu evaluation remains fragmented. This review synthesised 40 empirical studies published between 2013 and 2025 using descriptive mapping, cross-tabulation, and thematic synthesis. The findings showed that research has been concentrated on a limited set of dominant combinations, particularly radial menus used with ray-casting, and that evaluation has relied mainly on accuracy and task-completion time. Ergonomic indicators, including workload, comfort, fatigue, and cybersickness, received less consistent attention. The review further showed that current evaluation practice remains more developed for short-term performance than for long-term ergonomic quality. The findings indicate that VR menu evaluation should move beyond efficiency alone and adopt a more comprehensive perspective that considers menu type, interaction method, and performance metrics together to better support usable, ergonomically sustainable interface design.

items.abstract: This version corrects a citation error. Five passages on chaotic regularization in recurrent spiking networks cited the identifier 2606.04428, which belongs to an unrelated astrophysics paper on fast-spinning black holes; the passages describe arXiv:2606.04426 (Discrete signaling mediates chaotic regularization in recurrent neural networks), and all five now cite it. The wording of the claims is unchanged. Mathematical symbols that the previous PDF failed to render are now typeset. This version corrects specific citation errors found by an automated check and confirmed by hand; it has not had a full claim-by-claim audit. The full list of corrections is at the top of the PDF. Multi-step inference in large language models (LLMs) is typically evaluated at the level of final-answer accuracy, a metric that conflates many distinct failure modes: failures of decomposition, failures of integration, failures of analogical transfer, and failures of representational fidelity. This paper proposes a candidate framework, offered as a heuristic reading, not a formal derivation, in which compositional consistency serves as a unifying diagnostic axis for understanding where and why multi-step inference breaks down. We synthesize five to seven findings from recent arXiv preprints spanning cs.CL and q-bio.NC: (1) operadic consistency as a label-free, decomposition-sensitive accuracy predictor across twelve LLMs (arXiv:2606.13649, arXiv:2606.13634); (2) reasoning-aware analogical retrieval as a complementary training signal orthogonal to reward design (arXiv:2606.13680); (3) latent continuous-thought frameworks that aim to preserve probabilistic structure while bypassing discrete verbalization bottlenecks (arXiv:2606.06447); (4) constructional semantics acquisition as evidence that form-meaning compositionality emerges late and correlates with broader world-knowledge gains (arXiv:2605.31586); (5) neural representational geometry findings showing that chaotic recurrent networks produce smooth global population codes despite local roughness (arXiv:2606.04426); and (6) the variance allocation problem in brain foundation models, where higher-order co-skewness statistics, not captured by standard pretraining objectives, predict cognition better than second-order covariance alone (arXiv:2606.04010). Together these findings suggest, heuristically, that compositional consistency may track a structural property of inference simultaneously relevant to neural population geometry, language acquisition dynamics, and retrieval-augmented reasoning, though the cross-domain bridges are analogical, not mechanistic. The primary falsification path: if operadic consistency scores fail to predict accuracy on tasks requiring non-decomposable holistic inference (e.g., gestalt perceptual reasoning), the proposed axis would require revision or restriction to decomposition-structured tasks. items.title: Compositional Consistency as a Diagnostic Axis: How Operadic Structure, Analogical Retrieval, Latent Reasoning, Constructional Semantics, and Neural Representational Geometry Jointly Constrain Multi-Step Inference in Language Models
items.abstract: This version corrects a citation error. Five passages on chaotic regularization in recurrent spiking networks cited the identifier 2606.04428, which belongs to an unrelated astrophysics paper on fast-spinning black holes; the passages describe arXiv:2606.04426 (Discrete signaling mediates chaotic regularization in recurrent neural networks), and all five now cite it. The wording of the claims is unchanged. Mathematical symbols that the previous PDF failed to render are now typeset. This version corrects specific citation errors found by an automated check and confirmed by hand; it has not had a full claim-by-claim audit. The full list of corrections is at the top of the PDF. Multi-step inference in large language models (LLMs) is typically evaluated at the level of final-answer accuracy, a metric that conflates many distinct failure modes: failures of decomposition, failures of integration, failures of analogical transfer, and failures of representational fidelity. This paper proposes a candidate framework, offered as a heuristic reading, not a formal derivation, in which compositional consistency serves as a unifying diagnostic axis for understanding where and why multi-step inference breaks down. We synthesize five to seven findings from recent arXiv preprints spanning cs.CL and q-bio.NC: (1) operadic consistency as a label-free, decomposition-sensitive accuracy predictor across twelve LLMs (arXiv:2606.13649, arXiv:2606.13634); (2) reasoning-aware analogical retrieval as a complementary training signal orthogonal to reward design (arXiv:2606.13680); (3) latent continuous-thought frameworks that aim to preserve probabilistic structure while bypassing discrete verbalization bottlenecks (arXiv:2606.06447); (4) constructional semantics acquisition as evidence that form-meaning compositionality emerges late and correlates with broader world-knowledge gains (arXiv:2605.31586); (5) neural representational geometry findings showing that chaotic recurrent networks produce smooth global population codes despite local roughness (arXiv:2606.04426); and (6) the variance allocation problem in brain foundation models, where higher-order co-skewness statistics, not captured by standard pretraining objectives, predict cognition better than second-order covariance alone (arXiv:2606.04010). Together these findings suggest, heuristically, that compositional consistency may track a structural property of inference simultaneously relevant to neural population geometry, language acquisition dynamics, and retrieval-augmented reasoning, though the cross-domain bridges are analogical, not mechanistic. The primary falsification path: if operadic consistency scores fail to predict accuracy on tasks requiring non-decomposable holistic inference (e.g., gestalt perceptual reasoning), the proposed axis would require revision or restriction to decomposition-structured tasks. items.title: Cool Embeddings: Predicting Galaxy Cluster Cooling Times in IllustrisTNG and TNG-Cluster with AstroCLIP
items.abstract: Foundation models trained on optical astronomical data have not previously been applied to X-ray cluster thermodynamics. We show that embeddings from AstroCLIP, a contrastive vision-language model trained on optical galaxy images and spectra, retain physically meaningful structure when applied to mock Chandra X-ray images of simulated galaxy clusters - a significant shift in observational modality and physical scale. We target the central cooling time ($t_{\mathrm{cool},0}$) of the intracluster medium, a key diagnostic of cluster thermodynamics traditionally requiring X-ray spectroscopy. We present a machine learning framework that predicts $t_{\mathrm{cool},0}$ directly from X-ray images, applied to 711 projections from TNG300 and 993 from TNG-Cluster from the IllustrisTNG simulations. AstroCLIP embeddings form a structured latent space in which clusters with similar thermodynamic properties are naturally grouped, with no equivalent separation by halo mass. Building on this, we introduce a dot-product $k$-nearest neighbour attention model that retrieves similar clusters from the training set and adaptively reweights their cooling times. This model achieves root-mean-square errors of 0.24 (TNG300) and 0.23 (TNG-Cluster) in $\log(t_{\mathrm{cool},0})$, and demonstrates strong out-of-distribution generalisation, outperforming a fine-tuned convolutional neural network trained on raw images (RMSE 0.50 versus 0.73). These results demonstrate that pretrained foundation model embeddings transfer across astrophysical domains and encode thermodynamic information sufficient for inference of cluster cooling properties - offering a scalable path toward cool-core characterisation in all-sky surveys such as eROSITA.

items.title: Coordination and leadership: The impact of artificial intelligence
items.abstract: Coordination failure is an obstacle to collective efficiency in many economic and social settings. Leadership can attenuate this problem by providing a focal point through public communication. Yet, the effectiveness of such communication relies on shared trust that the leader’s recommendations will be followed by others. As generative artificial intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly accessible, leaders may use AI-generated texts in their public communications. Whether transparent AI assistance weakens the coordinating role of leadership remains an open question. We investigate this issue through an online experiment based on the minimum effort game with leadership. Leaders could send either a human-written or a ChatGPT-generated message, and followers were informed of the message’s source. Results reveal that coordination outcomes do not differ across treatments: AI-generated and human-written messages are equally effective in promoting coordination on the Pareto-dominant equilibrium. In addition, both leaders’ and followers’ beliefs about other players’ behavior are unaffected by the source of the message. These findings suggest a leader’s transparent choice to communicate through AI-generated messages does not undermine strategic communication or followers’ trust in successful coordination.

items.title: Coordination Under Pressure: How Topology Coupling, Fairness Constraints, Censored Feedback, Deliberation Failure, and Communication Efficiency Jointly Define a Candidate Design Framework for Scalable Multi-Agent Coordination
items.abstract: This version corrects a wrong arXiv identifier and removes the results of a withdrawn preprint. Version 2 cited the CONCAT framework as arXiv:2605.29511, which is a different paper (DynaGraph); CONCAT is arXiv:2605.29612, and all three citations are corrected. CONCAT was then withdrawn by its authors on 2026-09-22, who wrote: "We identified a potential issue in the repeated-run evaluation of our method that may have caused unintended prompt overlap across runs and affected the reported results. We therefore withdraw the manuscript for further investigation and re-evaluation". Version 2 used CONCAT's reported results (up to 2.02x higher efficiency and a 50.1% latency reduction) in Section 2.3 and as corroboration for the communication-entropy claim in Section 3.5. Those results are removed; that claim now rests on a single study, and the text says so. The five-mechanism thesis and the seven retained papers are unchanged. Typographic dashes are removed, Greek letters and mathematical symbols now render in the PDF, and the file carries a neutral name. The abstract below is unchanged apart from punctuation. The problems were found by an automated check and confirmed by hand against arXiv; this version has not had a full claim-by-claim audit. Multi-agent systems (MAS) are increasingly deployed at scales where coordination quality, not individual agent capability, becomes the primary performance bottleneck. This paper synthesises seven specific findings from recent arXiv preprints across cs.MA, cs.DC, and cs.NI to argue a candidate structural thesis: scalable multi-agent coordination is constrained by five interlocking mechanisms, topology-memory coupling, fairness-exploitability duality, censored-feedback identifiability, deliberation error propagation, and communication entropy, and that optimising any one in isolation predictably degrades the others. This is a heuristic reading, not a formal derivation; the sources share vocabulary and structural analogies but not a unified formalism, and the cross-domain bridges are argued by analogy rather than by shared mechanism. The corpus spans agent-based simulation, multi-agent reinforcement learning, LLM-based MAS, distributed network systems, and cooperative game theory. Key findings include: memory depth and network topology interact non-monotonically in LLM consensus formation arXiv:2606.04197; fair cooperative MARL policies are systematically exploitable unless contention geometry is carefully structured arXiv:2606.06162; censored feedback in threshold-cooperative tasks creates an identifiability problem that dominates coordination regret under the specific binary-censorship structure studied arXiv:2605.27076; deliberative consensus in multi-agent oracles degrades accuracy below single-model baselines on prediction market questions due to error propagation arXiv:2605.30802; and communication entropy reduction can be embedded as a training objective without sacrificing task performance in the MARL benchmarks studied arXiv:2606.07200. Two additional sources provide structural context: the compliance-correction symmetry in linear adversarial workflows on HumanEval arXiv:2606.12709 and the topology-dependent horizon trade-off in self-organised railway traffic arXiv:2606.13068. A further source, the Librarian study arXiv:2605.27787, is retained in a weakly-connected addendum; its connection to the communication entropy claim is analogical rather than mechanistic. The falsification path for the central thesis is concrete: if a MAS architecture independently optimises topology, fairness, feedback observability, deliberation protocol, and communication budget and achieves Pareto improvement across all five axes simultaneously, the interlocking-constraint claim is falsified. items.title: Correctness Debt at the Execution Boundary: How Type-System Gaps, Semantic Ambiguity, Harness Lifecycle Debt, Format Divergence, and Verification Theater Jointly Define a Structural Deficit in Deployed Software Infrastructure
items.abstract: This version (2026-09-26) corrects a citation error found by an automated check and confirmed by hand against the arXiv abstracts. Version 2 cited the identifier 2607.07314, an unrelated federated-learning paper posted after this synthesis was drafted, for the quantum software debugging paper that notes quantum bugs "often yield silent, incorrect outputs rather than explicit errors". That paper is arXiv:2606.07314 (QBugLM); all three citations are corrected, and its duplicate appearance in the list of papers dropped during selection is removed. The thesis is unchanged. This version has not had a full claim-by-claim audit. The full list of corrections is at the top of the PDF. Modern software infrastructure accumulates what we term correctness debt: a class of defects that are not random bugs but structural properties of the deployment pipeline itself, properties that testing and monitoring rarely catch because the failure mode is either silent, pre-runtime, or masked by a layer that was supposed to prevent it. This paper synthesizes five specific findings from recent cs.SE, cs.PL, and cs.AR preprints into a candidate reading of why correctness debt is growing faster than the tools meant to address it. The thesis is a heuristic reading, not a derivation: the five mechanisms are analogous in structure but do not share a single formal framework, and the analogy could be falsified by showing the mechanisms are causally independent in practice. The five mechanisms are: (1) type systems that cannot enforce resource-ownership invariants at compile time, leaving cost-bearing values aliasable at runtime arXiv:2606.04056; (2) undefined behavior that executes silently in production C/C++ code, generating thousands of warnings even under routine desktop tasks arXiv:2606.12064; (3) numeric format proliferation across ML accelerators that produces silent divergence without a shared bit-exact reference arXiv:2606.09686; (4) SBOM tooling that cannot agree on what a component is, leaving supply-chain blind spots even when all tools are run arXiv:2606.02442; and (5) harness lifecycle debt in LLM-agent systems, where structural defects mask task-level error signals and make conventional monitoring unreliable arXiv:2606.02494. The unifying structural pattern is verification theater: each layer nominally provides a correctness guarantee, but the guarantee is either non-enforceable, scope-limited, or defeated by the layer below it. The falsification path for the thesis is concrete: instrument a single production deployment with all five detection mechanisms simultaneously and measure whether the failure-mode categories are statistically independent, using a chi-squared test of co-occurrence with α = 0.05 as the threshold. If they cluster (reject independence), the structural-deficit framing is supported; if they are independent (fail to reject), the thesis reduces to five unrelated engineering problems. items.title: Counting on Thinking: Tracing Evidence Integration in Language Models
items.abstract: Finite computational resources force a tradeoff between automatic System 1 processes and costly System 2 thinking. Large language models (LLMs) can spend extra computation on hard problems, yet direct answers struggle even with counting, an elementary operation humans and animals perform automatically. We ask why this requires thinking in LLMs. Evidence integration has long been used in psychology and neuroscience to probe decision-making. Our evidence-integration task presents one letter per conversational turn and asks which of two target letters appeared more often. A running count difference solves the task optimally by weighting every letter equally; tokens at each turn could represent and update this difference. Direct responses instead weighted evidence unevenly, with strong recency effects, and assigned less probability to the correct answer as difficulty increased. Thinking improved performance and made integration weights nearly uniform, yet final-query attention remained concentrated on the sequence ends in both modes. Reasoning trajectories showed models revisiting input, recounting letters, and checking intermediate counts that informed the answer, suggesting that thinking constructs the accumulated count that direct responses lack rather than reading out one already formed. Reasoning-token costs grew with the number of letters far more than with coherence. Outcome feedback did not bring this computation into direct responses: under in-context reinforcement learning (ICRL), performance deteriorated over repeated games and recency effects strengthened, yet models grew more confident. items.title: Critical Evaluation of AI-Generated Academic Information in Higher Education: Empirical Evidence on Trust, AI-Related Digital Literacy and Verification Behaviour
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly used by university students for academic information seeking, explanation, drafting and problem solving. Its usefulness, however, depends not only on ease of use or frequency of interaction but also on users' capacity to evaluate and verify AI-generated information. This study presents an independent secondary-data analysis of a publicly available, anonymised dataset containing responses from 104 university students to 20 five-point Likert-scale items covering perceived ease of use (PEOU), trust in AI, verification behaviour and digital literacy. The analysis examined internal consistency, factorability diagnostics, descriptive statistics, Pearson correlations and multiple linear regression using heteroscedasticity-consistent HC3 standard errors. The four constructs demonstrated acceptable to high internal consistency (Cronbach's α = .782–.898). The KMO measure was .836 and Bartlett's test of sphericity was statistically significant, χ²(190) = 1087.35, p < .001, indicating that the item correlation matrix was suitable for factor-analytic examination. Verification behaviour was positively correlated with AI-related digital literacy (r = .445, p < .001), whereas its bivariate associations with PEOU and trust were not statistically significant. In the multivariable model, AI-related digital literacy showed the largest standardized coefficient (β = .524, p < .001). Trust showed a small negative adjusted association with verification behaviour (β = −.214, p = .048), whereas PEOU and usage frequency were not statistically significant. The model explained 25.3% of the variance in verification behaviour (R² = .253; adjusted R² = .223). The findings suggest that effective academic engagement with GenAI should not be equated with frequent use or perceived ease of use. Instead, evaluative digital-literacy capabilities appear particularly relevant to verification behaviour. Building on these findings, the study proposes the HEAVEN framework (Human-centred Evaluation of AI-generated academic information through Verification, Evidence and Nuanced judgement) as a conceptual framework integrating AI literacy, information verification, evidence appraisal and human judgement in higher education.

Intravenous thrombolysis is limited to 4.5 hours, but in India >90% patients present late after 8-12 hours. Objective: 1) To explain CTP physics, 2) To show how CTP extends window from 4.5 hr to 24 hr using Core-Penumbra mismatch, 3) To highlight potential AI bias when AI Trained on Foreign Data auto-perfusion software is applied to Indian population. Methods: This V1 is 100% synthetic educational model only. No patient data, no real CTP scans. All figures are schematic. Protocol: Step 1 NCCT Head to exclude hemorrhage, Step 2 CTA Head and Neck to see LVO ICA/M1, Step 3 CTP. Parameters: 40-50 ml contrast at 5 ml/sec, 60-70 sec scanning at 80 kVp. Four maps: CBF <30% = Core (Dead Brain - Blue Center), CBV low in Core, MTT >6 sec = Penumbra, Tmax >6 sec = Penumbra (At-Risk - Red Yellow Around). Results: Illustrative Hypothetical Synthetic Case (100% Educational - No Real Patient): *Concept: - Core <70 ml = Dead part small - operation possible - Penumbra = At Risk Part - can be saved - Mismatch Ratio = Penumbra / Core >1.8 = Savable part 1.8 times bigger than dead - good - Mismatch Volume >15 ml = At least 15 ml savable tissue must be there *Hypothetical Example (Synthetic Only): A hypothetical patient presents after 8 hours. NCCT Head is normal (plain black-white CT shows nothing common in early stroke). CTP shows Core 25 ml (dead brain part small blue in center cannot be saved) and Penumbra 110 ml (at risk big red-yellow around can be saved if blood returns quickly). Ratio = 110/25 = 4.4 which means savable 4 times more than dead. So even after 8 hours, thrombectomy (clot removal operation) can be done. *Note: This is 100% synthetic schematic calculation for teaching only, not a real case. Simple Tree Example: Core is dry dead tree in middle (Dead - cannot save). Penumbra is green trees around it drying but still alive (Can be saved if water / blood given quickly). Where AI is Used: CT detector hardware -> DAS -> CPU/GPU runs AI to make auto maps (RAPID type). Software reported trained on more than 50 perfusion studies from multiple sites (manufacturer reports larger internal datasets; we mention more than 50 with scientific caution). Since training mainly on AI Trained on Foreign Data, bias MAY exist for Indian pattern. Therefore, AI Trained on Foreign Data may need local Indian validation. V2 will test with real de-identified cases with IRB approval. Conclusion: CTP with Core-Penumbra mismatch can extend window from 4.5 hr to 24 hr and opens platform for next-generation medicine design. Introduction: AIS is sudden block in brain artery due to clot. This V1 is 100% CT based for practical Indian emergency use (Fast 5 min, available in 90% hospitals, low cost 4000-6000 Rs) as per DEFUSE-3 and DAWN which extended window to 24 hours. Tree Example: Core is dry dead tree in middle (cannot save). Penumbra is green trees around it drying but alive. Discussion - Drug Design and Development Vision: Educational Note: All investigational agents mentioned below are cited solely as EXAMPLES OF INVESTIGATIONAL DRUG DESIGN CLASSES to illustrate how CTP can serve as quantitative imaging biomarker / measurement tool in future trials as per FDA guidance on enrichment criteria where CTP mismatch is used as inclusion criteria. No dosage, no formulation, no route, no efficacy, no safety, no promotional claim is made. No commercial product is endorsed. This V1 is synthetic educational model only. 1. Need for New Medicine: Current standard thrombolytic works only within 4.5 hours, after that bleeding risk high. 2. New Medicine Classes Under Design (Examples only): - Class 1: Next-generation single-bolus thrombolytics (Example molecule class: tenecteplase-type plasminogen activators) - Class 2: Neuroprotectants / Cell-death pathway inhibitors (Example molecule class: PSD-95 inhibitor type such as NA-1 class agents) - Class 3: Anti-reperfusion injury modulators (Post-recanalization edema/inflammation modulators) 3. items.title: Darkness in the sun?: Imagining a solar energy future in Sierra Leone
items.abstract: Sierra Leone is faced with complex energy challenges, including very low rates of access to electricity. Nevertheless, ambitious goals have been set for the country through the Energy Transition and Green Growth Plan. Opportunities for solar energy deployment feature prominently in these goals, although they are clearly imagined in very different ways by the various energy sector actors. Some see large-scale hydropower as the future backbone of the electricity system, with opportunities for deploying solar photovoltaic energy in an auxiliary role. Others emphasise the potential of solar mini-grids. Still others see the greatest potential in household-scale solar systems to meet basic energy needs. In this article, we use the concept of sociotechnical imaginaries to examine these competing narratives. We argue that all of these technologies have their place in the future energy landscape of the country, but the vastly different geographical and economic realities and needs of diverse communities need to be duly considered when shaping the future energy landscape.

items.title: Deliberate Topology Selection as a First-Class Design Variable: How Multi-Agent Systems Learn When to Reconfigure, Prune, and Restructure Communication Graphs
items.abstract: This version corrects the synthesis after one of its sources was withdrawn. arXiv:2605.29612 (CONCAT) was withdrawn by its authors on 2026-09-22 because a potential issue in its repeated-run evaluation "may have caused unintended prompt overlap across runs and affected the reported results". The previous version used that preprint's efficiency and latency results as the evidence for its section on confidence-weighted pruning. Those results are removed, that section is now marked as an untested hypothesis, and the Abstract, Conclusion and Limitations note the withdrawal. The other findings are unchanged. This version corrects specific citation errors found by an automated check and confirmed by hand; it has not had a full claim-by-claim audit. The full list of corrections is at the top of the PDF. Multi-agent systems (MAS) built on large language models (LLMs) have converged on a common assumption: that the communication topology connecting agents is either fixed at design time or left entirely to unconstrained dynamic negotiation. This paper argues, through a heuristic reading of seven recent arXiv preprints spanning cs.MA, cs.DC, and cs.NI, that this binary is a false dichotomy, and that the most effective systems in the corpus share a structural pattern we call deliberate topology selection: the explicit, policy-guided choice of which edges to activate, suppress, or reconfigure at runtime, conditioned on task state, budget, and agent confidence. This is a heuristic reading, not a derivation from a shared formalism; the papers do not share a unified mathematical framework, but they converge on a common engineering diagnosis. The synthesis draws on findings about: training-free communication pruning via Theory-of-Mind confidence signals (arXiv:2605.29612) (a preprint its authors withdrew on 2026-09-22, so its reported results are not relied on here; see the Correction note); task-conditioned structural priors that guide posterior orchestration (arXiv:2605.25746); nucleus-electron hierarchies that separate stable backbones from dynamically activated agents (arXiv:2605.26178); game-theoretic minimax method selection under scenario uncertainty (arXiv:2606.02383); decentralized event-triggered synchronization under censored feedback (arXiv:2605.27076); federated market-based allocation over tree-structured service DAGs (arXiv:2605.27106); and infrastructure-layer topology proposals for V2X safety communication (arXiv:2605.25431). The central falsification path is concrete: if a static, task-agnostic topology trained once on a broad corpus consistently matches or outperforms deliberate topology selection across coordination-heavy benchmarks, the thesis collapses. The abstract reports no such result in any corpus paper; the claim remains a candidate structural pattern worth investigating, not an established law. items.title: Deliberate Topology Selection as a First-Class Design Variable: How Multi-Agent Systems Learn When to Reconfigure, Prune, and Restructure Communication Graphs
items.abstract: This version corrects the synthesis after one of its sources was withdrawn. arXiv:2605.29612 (CONCAT) was withdrawn by its authors on 2026-09-22 because a potential issue in its repeated-run evaluation "may have caused unintended prompt overlap across runs and affected the reported results". The previous version used that preprint's efficiency and latency results as the evidence for its section on confidence-weighted pruning. Those results are removed, that section is now marked as an untested hypothesis, and the Abstract, Conclusion and Limitations note the withdrawal. The other findings are unchanged. This version corrects specific citation errors found by an automated check and confirmed by hand; it has not had a full claim-by-claim audit. The full list of corrections is at the top of the PDF. Multi-agent systems (MAS) built on large language models (LLMs) have converged on a common assumption: that the communication topology connecting agents is either fixed at design time or left entirely to unconstrained dynamic negotiation. This paper argues, through a heuristic reading of seven recent arXiv preprints spanning cs.MA, cs.DC, and cs.NI, that this binary is a false dichotomy, and that the most effective systems in the corpus share a structural pattern we call deliberate topology selection: the explicit, policy-guided choice of which edges to activate, suppress, or reconfigure at runtime, conditioned on task state, budget, and agent confidence. This is a heuristic reading, not a derivation from a shared formalism; the papers do not share a unified mathematical framework, but they converge on a common engineering diagnosis. The synthesis draws on findings about: training-free communication pruning via Theory-of-Mind confidence signals (arXiv:2605.29612) (a preprint its authors withdrew on 2026-09-22, so its reported results are not relied on here; see the Correction note); task-conditioned structural priors that guide posterior orchestration (arXiv:2605.25746); nucleus-electron hierarchies that separate stable backbones from dynamically activated agents (arXiv:2605.26178); game-theoretic minimax method selection under scenario uncertainty (arXiv:2606.02383); decentralized event-triggered synchronization under censored feedback (arXiv:2605.27076); federated market-based allocation over tree-structured service DAGs (arXiv:2605.27106); and infrastructure-layer topology proposals for V2X safety communication (arXiv:2605.25431). The central falsification path is concrete: if a static, task-agnostic topology trained once on a broad corpus consistently matches or outperforms deliberate topology selection across coordination-heavy benchmarks, the thesis collapses. The abstract reports no such result in any corpus paper; the claim remains a candidate structural pattern worth investigating, not an established law. items.title: Deliberation Degrades, Aggregation Scales: How Multi-Agent Consensus Mechanisms Produce Divergent Reliability Profiles Across Coordination Topologies
items.abstract: This version removes evidence from a withdrawn preprint, found by an automated check and confirmed by hand. Version 2 used the CONCAT framework (arXiv:2605.29612) as evidence that pruning the agent communication graph recovers coordination quality. Its authors have withdrawn that preprint, stating: "We identified a potential issue in the repeated-run evaluation of our method that may have caused unintended prompt overlap across runs and affected the reported results. We therefore withdraw the manuscript for further investigation and re-evaluation". Every claim that rested on CONCAT is removed, the count of synthesised findings drops from 7 to 6, and the topology-adaptation argument now rests on two papers only (DynaGraph and AgensFlow), which makes it weaker than version 2 presented it. Typographic dashes are also removed. This version has not had a full claim-by-claim audit. The correction note is at the top of the PDF. A recurring structural pattern across recent multi-agent systems (MAS) research is that the mechanism by which agents reach collective decisions, aggregation versus deliberation, produces systematically different reliability and scalability profiles, and that neither mechanism dominates unconditionally. This paper synthesises 6 findings from recent arXiv preprints spanning cs.MA, cs.DC, and cs.NI to argue that this divergence is not incidental but is rooted in three interacting properties: (1) error correlation among agents, (2) the topology through which agents exchange information, and (3) the degree to which feedback signals are censored or delayed. We treat this as a heuristic reading across mechanistically distinct systems, not a derivation from a shared formal structure; the pattern is proposed, not proven. The core finding from prediction market oracle evaluation (arXiv:2605.30802) is the sharpest anchor: independent aggregation with confidence-weighted voting outperforms deliberative consensus, which degrades below single-model baselines, because deliberation propagates confident errors across agents whose outputs are already correlated (r = 0.529-0.689). This failure mode recurs in credit assignment for multi-agent prompt optimisation (arXiv:2605.30227) and in the censored-feedback coordination problem (arXiv:2605.27076). Complementary evidence from federated edge-cloud orchestration (arXiv:2605.27106) and dynamic topology reconfiguration (arXiv:2605.29511) suggests, by structural analogy, not direct equivalence, that topology-adaptive routing can recover coordination quality that static deliberation loses. The incremental voter model (arXiv:2605.28984) provides a mean-field analytic baseline for understanding how step-wise opinion updating in a fully-mixed topology converges or fails to converge under persuader bias; its connection to LLM deliberation is analogical and is treated as a weakly-connected addendum. The falsification path for the central claim is concrete: construct a benchmark where agent error correlation is experimentally varied from near-zero to near-one while holding task difficulty constant; if deliberative consensus degrades monotonically with correlation while aggregation does not, the mechanism is confirmed. If both degrade similarly, the topology assumption is the confound. Authorship: Saluca Agentic AI Research Team (Saluca LLC). items.title: DEVELOPING STUDENTS' SPEAKING SKILLS THROUGH ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE: EDUCATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES AND CURRENT CHALLENGES
items.abstract: This study examines the role, educational opportunities, and current challenges of integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies into higher education to develop university students' oral communication and foreign language speaking skills. Utilizing natural language processing (NLP), automatic speech recognition (ASR), and large language models (LLMs), the paper establishes a theoretical and practical framework for AI-mediated instruction. Key benefits, such as reducing foreign language speaking anxiety, constructing personalized learning trajectories, offering real-time corrective feedback, and enhancing phonetic accuracy and oral fluency, are analyzed in detail. Furthermore, the paper highlights critical implementation barriers and provides actionable pedagogical guidelines for incorporating AI applications effectively into tertiary curricula.

items.title: Digital Transformation of Indian Commerce and the Changing World of Work: A Conceptual Review of Business, Employment and Workforce Capability
items.abstract: This conceptual review examines how digital transformation is reshaping Indian commerce and the world of work that sustains it. Adopting an integrative literature review design, the study synthesises 30 scholarly and institutional sources, comprising foundational theory on technology and organisations, recent evidence on automation and artificial intelligence, and India-focused research and official reports on digitalisation, employment, informality and leadership, through thematic analysis. Four themes emerge: the digitalisation of commercial activity, the recomposition of employment, the centrality of workforce capability and leadership, and the risk of a widening divide between the organised economy and traditional and unorganised sectors. Official estimates place India's digital economy at 11.74% of national income in 2022-23, with a projected share of nearly one-fifth by 2029-30, which underlines the scale of the shift. The synthesis indicates that the employment effects of digitalisation are compositional and not uniformly negative, that returns to digital investment depend on complementary human and organisational capabilities, and that the informal workforce, including handloom producers, construction labour and migrant workers, remains largely outside the digital dividend. The paper integrates these insights into a Digital Commerce–Work–Capability framework and advances five research propositions for empirical testing. It offers practical guidance for business managers, educational institutions and policymakers seeking inclusive digital growth.

items.abstract: The processes in audit firms face operational challenges due to the reliance on manual workflows, particularly in managing audit engagement tasks and tracking auditor training hours. Such inefficiencies lead to an increased administrative burden and potential compliance risks. This work describes our initiatives to address these issues by developing a system that combines a web application to streamline audit engagement monitoring and a mobile application to monitor staff training. Initially designed to replace manual workflows, the system has evolved to incorporate generative artificial intelligence to enhance knowledge retrieval for audit-related queries. The initiatives improve the efficiency of audit engagement and staff training monitoring, enabling audit firms to achieve significant improvements in their workflow.

items.abstract: The processes in audit firms face operational challenges due to the reliance on manual workflows, particularly in managing audit engagement tasks and tracking auditor training hours. Such inefficiencies lead to an increased administrative burden and potential compliance risks. This work describes our initiatives to address these issues by developing a system that combines a web application to streamline audit engagement monitoring and a mobile application to monitor staff training. Initially designed to replace manual workflows, the system has evolved to incorporate generative artificial intelligence to enhance knowledge retrieval for audit-related queries. The initiatives improve the efficiency of audit engagement and staff training monitoring, enabling audit firms to achieve significant improvements in their workflow.

items.title: Dynamic response and energy dissipation of different soil media under touchdown impact of collapsed bodies: Field experiments and numerical simulations
items.abstract: Ground deformation induced by the touchdown impact of collapsed bodies can adversely affect critical structures and facilities, including adjacent buildings, underground pipelines, and metro tunnels. This study investigates the soil deformation induced by collapsed body impact in two typical strata, namely homogeneous soil and stiff-over-soft strata. We conducted model tests for both strata, and established an experimentally validated numerical model using the LS-DYNA finite element analysis software. We analysed the dynamic response characteristics and energy dissipation patterns of both homogeneous soil and stiff-over-soft strata models under the most unfavorable working conditions of touchdown impact loading. Two methods, namely the force–displacement curve method and the Winkler foundation model, were adopted to predict the energy dissipation during the touchdown impact process. Research findings indicated that the dynamic response characteristics of homogeneous soil models under touchdown impact loading were significantly influenced by distance and depth. The majority (approximately 83.37%) is of the impact energy dissipated through plastic deformation of the soil. In stiff-over-soft strata, due to the confinement effect and ’shell effect’ of the concrete slab, localised failure and crack propagation within the slab dominate system energy dissipation, accounting for approximately 61.63% of the total impact energy. When employing force–displacement curves to predict energy dissipation in models directly subjected to impact, both models demonstrated good agreement with simulation results. However, when using the Winkler foundation model to predict energy dissipation in directly impacted models, the homogeneous soil model showed superior agreement. These findings can provide a valuable reference for the safety assessment and the formulation of protective measures for engineering structures affected by the touchdown impact loading of collapsed bodies.

items.title: Dynamics of Temporary Cognitive Lapses in Large Language Models and Human Cognitive Pulse Interventions: The Topology of Co-Evolutionary Intelligence
items.abstract: This study establishes a rigorous mathematical and empirical framework governing the transient state-space deviations from deterministic logical trajectories---conceptually designated as temporary cognitive lapses---observed in Large Language Models (LLMs) under extended context horizons. Grounded in a functionalist paradigm that transitions human-AI interaction into a single, closed-loop symbiotic informatics matrix, we define these lapses as volatile log-probability fluctuations triggered by localized attention hyperpolarization across supersaturated symbolic fields. Unlike permanent structural hallucinations, the real-time injection of human-guided subsegmentation commands operates as an exogenous homeostatic forcing operator---termed a cognitive pulse. This external impulse perturbs the key-value (KV) cache history matrix via entry-wise Hadamard modulation, forcing an exact singular value condensation that flattens distorted log-probability landscapes. Consequently, the diffuse probability mass is compressed, executing an instantaneous non-continuous vertical trajectory jump that re-orients the hidden representation vectors back onto canonical factual state attractors. We provide quantitative theoretical predictions tracking these transitions across all operational co-evolutionary interaction phases, establishing a rigorous mathematical baseline for co-evolutionary intelligence survival. items.title: Economic Governance of Autonomous Agents and Robots: Factor-Origin Accounting and Social Automation Funds
items.abstract: Contemporary fiscal architectures rely overwhelmingly on human labor income and payroll withholdings to finance social insurance and public infrastructure. The rapid diffusion of autonomous software agents, generative foundation models, and embodied robotic systems decouples output growth from human work hours, eroding traditional tax bases while exacerbating capital-income concentration. Prevailing policy proposals, ranging from uniform robot levies to unconditional cash transfers, fail to resolve three foundational challenges: attributing economic value across mixed human-machine workflows, establishing legal fiscal liability without creating fictional machine personhood, and building an equitable distribution mechanism that converts technological surplus into durable public wealth. This paper presents CivicDividendOS, an end-to-end computational fiscal framework for mixed human-AIrobot economies. The architecture introduces an Autonomous Economic Activity Passport (AEAP) that anchors machine activity to accountable corporate beneficiaries, paired with a Factor-Origin Ledger (FOL) that calculates causal marginal contributions across labor, AI services, robotics, data, and conventional capital. Drawing on an endogenous Substitution-Augmentation Classifier, the system levies a dynamic Social Automation Contribution (SAC) on automated value added, offering explicit offset credits for worker upskilling, augmentation, and task innovation. Accrued revenues are recycled through a Human Earned-Income Shield (HEIS) to reduce payroll wedges and a Public Automation Wealth Fund (PAWF) whose structural yields endow citizen dividends, transition insurance, and human capabilities. We formalize the mathematical architecture, illustrate its operation in an urban logistics setting, and outline an evaluation protocol via a macroeconomic policy digital twin.

items.title: EEG-Based Motor Imagery BCI Algorithms and Technologies: A Review
items.abstract: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) have emerged as transformative technologies that enable direct communication between the brain and external devices. Among various BCI paradigms, EEG-based motor imagery (MI) has gained prominence due to its simplicity, non-invasiveness, and potential to restore motor function and facilitate rehabilitation for patients with motor impairments. This paper presents a comprehensive review of the most practical processing algorithms developed over the past decade for decoding brain sensorimotor cortex signals. Specifically, this paper discusses the integration of artificial intelligence (AI)-based algorithms, particularly machine learning and deep learning techniques, and their contributions to improving the performance and efficiency of MI-BCI systems in detail. Furthermore, the paper reviews state-of-the-art hardware platforms and emerging converging technologies, including system-on-chip (SoC) architectures, application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs), field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs), wearable devices, the Internet of Things (IoT), and augmented/virtual reality (AR/VR), and discusses their integration with advanced signal processing algorithms to enable next-generation MI-BCI systems. By highlighting current achievements of EEG-based MI-BCI technology and predicting future research directions that could further enhance real-time capabilities, this paper aims to provide valuable insights for researchers and practitioners, fostering innovation in high-performance EEG-based MI-BCI systems.

items.title: El analfabetismo de agencia: La ilusión de la destreza técnica frente a la pérdida de autogobierno
items.abstract: Este ensayo examina la discrepancia entre la alfabetización técnica en inteligencia artificial y la preservación del juicio deliberativo, introduciendo el concepto de analfabetismo de agencia. Frente a marcos normativos como el Artículo 4 del Reglamento de Inteligencia Artificial de la Unión Europea, se analiza la falacia del «human-in-the-loop» como un mecanismo de legitimación burocrática y exculpación jurídica mediante el análisis empírico del sistema MCAS del Boeing 737 MAX. Finalmente, se proponen dos salvaguardas operativas indispensables para el autogobierno sociotécnico: la reserva operacional y el oficio de responder. ---This essay examines the gap between technical artificial intelligence literacy and the preservation of deliberative judgment, introducing the concept of agency illiteracy. In light of regulatory frameworks such as Article 4 of the European Union Artificial Intelligence Act, it analyzes the fallacy of the "human-in-the-loop" as an instrument of bureaucratic legitimation and legal exculpation through the empirical case of the Boeing 737 MAX MCAS system. Finally, it proposes two indispensable operational safeguards for sociotechnical self-governance: operational reserve and the craft of answering (moral accountability).

items.title: El ensayo de suficiencia: Metodología de auditoría por sustracción, diseño institucional y preservación de la agencia en sistemas sociotécnicos mediados
items.abstract: Este trabajo formaliza el ensayo de suficiencia como un protocolo de auditoría sociotécnica concebido para verificar la autonomía operativa y el discernimiento deliberativo en entornos de alta mediación computacional. Frente a métricas convencionales que premian la velocidad del binomio humano–máquina bajo asistencia ininterrumpida, se fundamenta el principio de «evaluación por sustracción» con salvaguardas explícitas de contención de riesgo. Se reelabora la noción de competencia parasitaria no como una deficiencia individual o culposa del operador, sino como una propiedad emergente de configuraciones institucionales que incentivan la delegación epistémica y restringen el acceso a los fundamentos del sistema. A partir de los marcos de la ingeniería de resiliencia (Hollnagel, Woods) y de la práctica de la ingeniería del caos ya consolidada en sistemas distribuidos, el ensayo desarrolla un protocolo estructurado en cuatro vectores normativos —continuidad esencial, degradación comprensible, suficiencia material y agencia verificable—, contextualiza el caso histórico del MCAS en la aviación civil como referencia documental sobre asimetría informativa y degradación inadvertida, y propone criterios de gobernanza aplicables a proyectos e infraestructuras críticas. ---This paper formalizes the "sufficiency test" as a sociotechnical auditing protocol designed to verify operational autonomy and deliberative judgment in highly mediated computational environments. In contrast to conventional performance metrics that reward human–machine throughput under continuous algorithmic assistance, it operationalizes the principle of "evaluation by subtraction" within explicit containment boundaries. The concept of parasitic competence is redefined not as an individual moral or technical failing, but as an emergent property of sociotechnical configurations that incentivize epistemic offloading while restricting structural access and deliberative authority. Grounded in resilience engineering frameworks (Hollnagel, Woods) and in the already-established practice of chaos engineering in distributed systems, the essay formulates a structured testing protocol across four normative vectors—essential continuity, understandable degradation, material sufficiency, and verifiable agency—, examines the MCAS civil aviation case as an illustrative documentary reference on information asymmetry and unannounced degradation, and outlines governance mechanisms for critical infrastructure and project management.
